analysis.evidence: כָּל הַחַיָּה אֲשֶׁר אִתְּךָ means “every living creature that is with you.” The command to bring them out includes every creature among the birds, livestock, and creeping things listed.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָּל הַחַיָּה אֲשֶׁר אִתְּךָ means “every living creature with you.” The verse includes birds, livestock, and everything that creeps on the ground among the creatures Noah is to bring out.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute noun with the definite article הַ־, used collectively after כָּל.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces the relative clause אֲשֶׁר אִתְּךָ, “that is with you,” which modifies כָּל הַחַיָּה, “every living creature.”
analysis.morphology: Indeclinable relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In מִכָּל בָּשָׂר, “of all flesh,” כֹּל modifies the collective noun בָּשָׂר. The following list of birds, livestock, and creeping things identifies the creatures included in “all flesh” here.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed preposition מִן. The נ assimilates to the following כ.

analysis.evidence: מִכָּל בָּשָׂר means “of all flesh.” The verse specifies the creatures Noah is to bring out with him: birds, livestock, and everything that creeps on the ground.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, used collectively, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: all flesh: every living creature; mankind

analysis.evidence: After מִכָּל בָּשָׂר (‘of all flesh’), בָּעוֹף stands alongside וּבַבְּהֵמָה (‘and among the livestock’) and וּבְכָל הָרֶמֶשׂ (‘and among all the creeping things’). Each phrase names a class of creatures Noah is to bring out.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ with the definite article, followed by a masculine singular absolute collective noun.

analysis.evidence: The verse lists birds, four-footed animals, and creeping things as groups within מִכָּל בָּשָׂר, “of all flesh.” The singular בְּהֵמָה names the four-footed animals collectively, with no restriction to livestock.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute common noun used collectively, with conjunction וּ־ and preposition בְּ־ combined with the definite article as בַּ־.

analysis.evidence: The preposition בְ repeats the pattern of בָּעוֹף וּבַבְּהֵמָה. כָל governs the definite collective הָרֶמֶשׂ, including all the creatures that creep on the ground.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ + preposition בְ + masculine singular construct noun כָל

analysis.evidence: After the birds and livestock, כָל הָרֶמֶשׂ names another group of animals Noah is to bring out. The following participle הָרֹמֵשׂ agrees with the collective noun in the masculine singular and describes how these creatures move about on the ground.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with the prefixed definite article הָ, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: הָרֹמֵשׂ agrees with the preceding masculine singular collective noun הָרֶמֶשׂ. The phrase עַל הָאָרֶץ specifies where the creatures move.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, with the definite article הָ־, used attributively.

analysis.evidence: In הָרֹמֵשׂ עַל הָאָרֶץ, “that creeps on the ground,” עַל introduces the surface on which the creature moves.
analysis.morphology: Simple preposition without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In הָרֶמֶשׂ הָרֹמֵשׂ עַל הָאָרֶץ, “the creeping thing that creeps on the ground,” עַל הָאָרֶץ identifies the surface on which the creature moves.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a common-gender singular noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: The command addresses Noah. כָּל הַחַיָּה אֲשֶׁר אִתְּךָ (“every living creature that is with you”) is its object, and אִתָּךְ (“with you”) specifies that Noah is to bring the creatures out of the ark with him.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil imperative, second person masculine singular. Initial הַ־ marks the verbal stem.

draft.change: Include the Qal sense with creatures as subject alongside the previously proposed sense with waters as subject and the related collective noun.
draft.evidence: Genesis 7:21 describes the creatures by their activity on the ground. Genesis 1:20 uses the same verb with the waters as subject.

article.summary: Waters teem with living creatures in Genesis 1:20. In Genesis 7:21 the creatures themselves swarm on the ground, and the related noun names them collectively.

senses.definition: Living creatures that swarm, taken collectively.

evidence.note: The noun names the living creatures with which the waters are to teem.
The singular noun covers the creatures that swarm on the ground.
The participle describes what the creatures do on the ground.

senses.definition: Of waters, to teem with living creatures.

evidence.note: The waters are commanded to teem with living creatures.
The verse describes the living creatures with which the waters teemed.

analysis.evidence: The creatures Noah is commanded to bring out are the subject of וְשָׁרְצוּ. בָאָרֶץ gives the place where they are to swarm, and וּפָרוּ וְרָבוּ continues with the same subject, “and be fruitful and multiply.”
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural, with prefixed וְ (weqatal) expressing the intended result of the command.

analysis.evidence: In וְשָׁרְצוּ בָאָרֶץ, the earth is where the animals are to swarm after leaving the ark. The parallel command to be fruitful and multiply עַל הָאָרֶץ confirms that בָאָרֶץ names the realm they are to repopulate.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ with the definite article, prefixed to a common noun, singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: God tells Noah to bring the animals out so that they may swarm on the earth. וּפָרוּ describes their producing offspring, and the paired verb וְרָבוּ describes their increase in number.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural, with prefixed conjunction וּ; the form continues the purpose of the preceding command.

analysis.evidence: The paired verbs וּפָרוּ וְרָבוּ describe the animals being brought out of the ark so that they may be fruitful and multiply on the earth. The increase is in the number of animals.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural, with prefixed וְ (weqatal), expressing the intended result of the command.

analysis.evidence: In וּפָרוּ וְרָבוּ עַל הָאָרֶץ, “be fruitful and multiply on the earth,” עַל introduces הָאָרֶץ as the place where the creatures are to multiply.
In וּפָרוּ וְרָבוּ עַל הָאָרֶץ, the earth is the realm where the creatures leaving the ark are to be fruitful and multiply.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, common gender, singular absolute, with prefixed definite article הָ־.
